reply.text:
Jumping is a **rule**, not something you write on the player directly.

Open your Player actor and look at its `use rule` rows. If `Jumps` is not among them, add it — that gives the actor a `jump` action and the properties behind it (`jump strength`, `coyote time`).

Then the player needs a reason to jump. In the same actor, add a handler for the event you want:

- `when Player is pressing up` → `Player jump`

If it already has the rule and still does not move, check that something is giving it gravity: `Falls` is a separate rule, and a jump with nothing pulling back down looks like nothing happening.

Scoring hangs off a collision, so two actors have to agree.

The coin needs the `Collectable` trait from the `Collection` rule, and the player needs `Collects`. Neither has to know about the other — that is what makes "these things can be picked up" sayable at all.

Then, on the Player, handle the event:

- `when Player collects ⟨thing⟩` → `add 1 to score`

If nothing happens, the usual cause is that one of the two actors is missing its half of the pair — check the `use rule` rows on both.

Look at the console under the game — a world says what went wrong there.

A message about reading a property of nothing almost always means a block is pointing at an actor that is not in the map, or one that was removed while a rule still held it. Check the actor-typed properties in your map: if a Health Bar's `subject` names an actor you deleted, it will be empty at run time.

fallback.text: This is a recorded conversation — there is no model behind it. Ask about jumping, about scoring, or about an error you are seeing, and I have an answer ready.
